de.my_domain.abalone.model

Interface Board

  • All Known Implementing Classes:
    Abalone

    public interface Board
    Interface for an Abalone (lite) game. A human plays against the machine. The human's ground lines are always the lowest rows, whereas the ground lines of the machine are the highest rows. The human plays from bottom to top, the machine from top to bottom. The user with the black balls opens the game. Winner is who first pushes out/eliminates six of the opponent's balls.

    There are some differences to traditional Abalone:

    • In case that one player has no option to make a valid move, he must miss a turn. The other player can make a move in any case.
    • A move can involve more than three (own) balls.
    • Sideward moves, i.e., changing the diagonal of more than one own ball not in the same row, are not allowed.
    • The game may never end.

      • move

        Board move(int rowFrom,
           int diagFrom,
           int rowTo,
           int diagTo)
        Executes a human move. Eliminating own balls is allowed. This method does not change the state of this instance, which is treated here as immutable. Instead, a new board/game is returned, which is a copy of this with the move executed.
        Parameters:
        rowFrom - The slot's row number from which the ball of the human player should be moved.
        diagFrom - The slot's diagonal number from which the ball of the human player should be moved.
        rowTo - The slot's row number to which the ball of the human player should be moved.
        diagTo - The slot's diagonal number to which the ball of the human player should be moved.
        Returns:
        A new board with the move executed. If the move is not valid, then null will be returned.
        Throws:
        java.lang.IllegalStateException - If the game is already over, or it is not the human's turn.
        java.lang.IllegalArgumentException - If the provided parameters are invalid, e.g., the from slot lies outside the grid or the to slot outside the grid plus an one-element border.

      • machineMove

        Board machineMove()
        Executes a machine move. This method does not change the state of this instance, which is treated here as immutable. Instead, a new board/game is returned, which is a copy of this with the move executed.

        Throws:

      • toString

        java.lang.String toString()
        Gets the string representation of this board as row x diagonals hexagon. Each slot is represented by one the three chars '.', 'X', or 'O'. '.' means that the slot currently contains no ball. 'X' means that it contains a black tile. 'O' means that it contains a white tile.
        Overrides:
        toString in class java.lang.Object
        Returns:
        The string representation of the current state of this game.
